stem: The economic growth demonstrated by this recruitment letter was primarily a result of —

options.label: F
options.text: the passage of strict federal labor laws

options.label: G
options.text: the abolition of the slave trade

options.label: H
options.text: the expansion of the cottage industry system

options.label: J
options.text: the new production methods of industrialization

visual_elements: "We can give employment to from 50 to 100 girls, at the usual wages paid in this place. Our custom is to pay to new hands one dollar per week, & board in the Weaving & Dressing Rooms, & one dollar & a half & board, in the Carding & Spinning Rooms, until they can tend the Machines without assistance. After that they are paid for all the work they can get off...." —John Clark, July 27, 1847
